Hello Council Members! First of all Lake City and I would like to give some input from my experience with rentable electric scooters. I recently was trying to get home from temple square so I grabbed a scooter. I walked it from the sidewalk onto the road (300 south), then got on. The difference in the speed of the scooter immediately made me feel very unsafe, because normally I can go 15 mph and am really able to share the road with the other cars without too many issues. But at the speed limit they have set, I feel like an obstruction and it also makes it much more dangerous because of the greater speed differential. I heard that you were behind this new rule about the scooter speed limits, so that's why I'm writing to you. From what I have read, it seems like the reasoning was that the city wanted slow vehicle road speed limits that don't apply to cars in the same area individually. I scooter can't go as fast as a car by mechanics, but it shouldn't be set up artificially slow. And second, I'd like to make sure that it's clear that people need proper education on scooter riders know how to properly share the road with cars and ride in a responsible way. I would never rely on the sidewalk as it is dangerous for pedestrians and for me as a scooter rider, and I would much rather be on the road. But it needs to be at a safe speed for everyone to maintain safety. If the speed limit is 7 mph, it makes me feel really discouraged and like I'm not trusted to operate the scooter as a responsible rider, as cars are. We should have proper rules for sharing on the sidewalk, yielding to pedestrians, and parking like scooters properly, but not these crazy low speed limits. Thanks for listening to my experience!
